section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Pillars
section_1.content: Briefly revisit differentiation as finding the slope (velocity) and integration as finding the area (total distance). Use a graphical animation showing a car's speedometer vs. odometer.
section_1.example: A delivery drone's velocity curve vs. its cumulative distance traveled.

section_2.title: The Conceptual Link: Accumulation Functions
section_2.content: Introduce the area function A(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t) dt. Visualize this as a 'sliding curtain' moving across a graph, covering area as 'x' increases.
section_2.example: A squirrel gathering nuts: The rate of gathering (nuts/minute) integrated over time gives the total nut pile size.

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1): The Inverse Relationship
section_3.content: Explain that the derivative of the accumulation function is the original function: d/dx [∫[a to x] f(t) dt] = f(x). Graphically demonstrate that the tiny change in area is just a narrow rectangular strip of height f(x).
section_3.example: If the rate of water flow into a tank is f(t), the rate of change of the tank's volume is exactly the current flow rate.

section_4.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 2): Evaluating Definite Integrals
section_4.content: Define the relationship: ∫[a to b] f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is the antiderivative. This connects the 'net change' to the 'anti-slope'.
section_4.example: A rocket's position at time 'b' minus its position at time 'a' equals the integral of its velocity function between those times.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude that differentiation and integration are reverse processes (inverse operations). Display a circular animation showing the transition from f(x) to F(x) and back.
section_5.example: A game character: Differentiation takes you from position to velocity; Integration takes you from velocity back to position.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to keep left side for lecture
                x = 2.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
